core_obligations: Obtain weak adicness and admissibility of the source, fix an ideal of definition of the source and a finitely generated ideal of definition of the target (proof lines 1899-1903).

Replace the target's ideal by a suitable power so that it lies in the closure of the extension of the chosen ideal, deduce the containment of the ideal in the sum of the extension and its square, and apply Nakayama's lemma to the finitely generated quotient to conclude that the target's ideal lies in the extension (proof lines 1903-1922).

Use finite generation to produce a finitely generated subideal of the chosen ideal whose extension contains the target's ideal, and use continuity and openness to get a power of the chosen ideal inside the target's ideal (proof lines 1924-1928).

Read the containment modulo the closure of a higher power, pass it through the faithfully flat map between the quotients, and iterate to show that the closures of the powers of the finitely generated subideal are open (proof lines 1928-1944).
Conclude by the criterion that the source is adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition (proof lines 1946-1948).
proof_roadmap: Weak adicness and admissibility, and the two ideals (proof lines 1899-1903).
Nakayama's lemma and the first containment (proof lines 1903-1922).
Lifting finite generation and a power containment (proof lines 1924-1928).
Iterated containments after a faithfully flat extension (proof lines 1928-1944).
Conclusion by the finite generation criterion (proof lines 1946-1948).
difficulty_reason: In the situation of the taut descent statements of the chapter, the lemma asserts that if the target ring is adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition and the source is complete, then the source has the same property (statement lines 1892-1897). The proof first obtains weak adicness and admissibility of the source from the corresponding descent statement, and fixes an ideal of definition of the source together with a finitely generated ideal of definition of the target (proof lines 1899-1903). A chain of reductions follows. Since the closure of the extension of the chosen ideal is open, a power of the target's ideal lies inside it, so after replacing that ideal by that power one may assume it is contained in the closure, which by the description of closures as intersections gives the containment of the ideal in the sum of the extension and its square; the quotient is then a finitely generated module on which the ideal acts as the identity, and because the ideal lies in the Jacobson radical, Nakayama's lemma forces that quotient to vanish, so the target's ideal is contained in the extension of the source's ideal (proof lines 1903-1922). Its finite generation then produces a finitely generated subideal of the chosen ideal of the source whose extension contains the target's ideal, and continuity together with openness gives a power of the chosen ideal inside the target's ideal (proof lines 1924-1928). The final step compares the two ideals modulo the closure of a higher power: the containment obtained above, read modulo that closure, passes through the faithfully flat map between the quotients to give a containment of powers in the source, which iterates to show that the closure of every power of the finitely generated subideal is open, whence the source is adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition by the corresponding criterion (proof lines 1928-1948). The claim is H3: the argument combines Nakayama's lemma applied to a finitely generated module, a lifting of finite generation from the extension back to the source, and an iteration of containments checked after a faithfully flat extension, and each of the three is a separate mechanism.
